problem: Heuristic, RL and end-to-end object-search methods generalize poorly to large-scale unstructured (outdoor) environments, and LLMs used for embodied search have weak 3D spatial grounding, no consistent decision-making, and no mechanism to store and reuse past search experience.
motivation: Object search in large outdoor or semi-open spaces, where objects and their surroundings correlate only loosely, needs semantic reasoning plus reuse of experience across repeated tasks. LLMs supply semantic priors, but their proposals are spatially unsafe or redundant and they cannot accumulate memory, so an external evaluator and an explicit probabilistic memory can compensate.
key_idea: Pair an LLM Proposer with an external rule-based Evaluator (DoUT) that ranks and gives feedback on candidate directions, and keep a GMM-based task probability map of past target locations for efficient repeated search.
insight: Moving critique out of the LLM into a parallel external Evaluator with mandatory (format) and advisory (safety, redundancy, direction-change) criteria compensates for the LLM's weak 3D awareness. It also cuts LLM calls: once converged DoUT needs 1 call per cycle versus 4 for DoT, and it stabilizes after 3–4 tasks versus 10–11 for DoT. The GMM memory further shortens paths and reduces variance in repeated tasks (Scene 1 path 390.41 → 353.67 m), and it also handles changed start and target. Real-world gains over heuristic explorers come mainly from LLM semantic priors, and no ablation isolates the GMM or Evaluator on real-robot search performance.
method: Semantic Octomap: panoramic images are segmented with Grounded-SAM and RAM, projected onto LiDAR points to form a semantic point cloud, and fused incrementally into an octomap with Bayesian occupancy and label updates.

DoUT reasoning: the panorama is split into N=11 direction segments (odd N to avoid oscillation); the LLM Proposer (GPT-4o-mini) outputs ranked candidate directions and an external Evaluator re-ranks them and returns structured feedback.

Evaluator criteria: mandatory criteria (output format, count mismatch) force re-generation; advisory score C_i = λ1·Order + λ2·security (quadratic obstacle penalty) + λ3·repeated-exploration overlap with sparse roadmap + λ4·(1−cos direction change), with λ=2.5/10/3/1.5.

Task Probability Map: one GMM per target category; on success add a Gaussian at the found location (σ² proportional to object size), merge with nearby components, renormalize weights so old data fades.

Experienced search: the GMM component means (or octomap cells labeled with the target category) become TSP nodes, with distances from A* and weighted by (1−βπ_j); if the tour fails it falls back to reasoning search.

Local target selection and fallback: top-ranked direction subject to reachability and continuous-movement rules; A* in the octomap; once unexplored coverage passes a threshold, TSP over roadmap regions with FAEL-style coverage.
Trajectory refinement: a rolling ESDF plus gradient-based trajectory optimization (Zhou et al. 2019) gives safe, smooth paths with dynamic-obstacle handling.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o-mini (frozen, prompted; also tested GPT-4o, LearnLM 1.5, Moonshot AI in DoUT alignment study)
setting.training_data: none (training-free; LLM adapts online via Evaluator feedback; GMM built from prior runs)
setting.observation: 360° panoramic RGB (Insta360 X4) + Livox Mid-360 LiDAR, FAST-LIO2 localization
setting.action_space: continuous local targets and A*/optimized trajectories for a two-wheeled self-balancing robot (max 1 m/s)

numbers_note: Only real-world, two-scene custom benchmarks with path length and time; no standard benchmark and no SR/SPL (all methods reported 100% success). The number of trials is not stated. DoUT vs DoT and multi-LLM alignment results are given only in figures (cosine similarity values partly in text).
results: In first-time search, GET cuts path length in Scene 1 to 390.41 m versus 521.81 m for the strongest baseline Sem (−25.2%) and 720.32 m for FAEL, and time to 412.40 s. In Scene 2 it reaches 191.97 m versus 380.60 m for FAEL. Experienced search further reduces this to 353.67 m and 179.88 m (same task), and stays low at 378.58 m and 186.19 m when start and target change, all with much lower variance than baselines.
limitations: Evaluation covers only two real-world scenes with a single robot; no standard benchmarks, no success-rate differentiation (all 100%), and no ablation of the Evaluator, GMM or DoUT on search performance.
Real-time operation depends on a cloud LLM over 4G and slow panoramic segmentation (~1.85 s), and reasoning search cannot guarantee coverage, requiring a fallback exhaustive exploration.
Evaluator weights and criteria are hand-designed, and the LLM only 'learns' to align with them (cosine similarity up to 0.91), not verified as better search decisions.
